title: Harmful effect of megadoses of vitamins: electroencephalogram abnormalities and seizures induced by intravenous folate in drug-treated epileptics
authors: Ch'ien LT, Krumdieck CL, Scott CW Jr, Butterworth CE Jr
population: Patients with epilepsy treated with phenytoin for more than 1 year, six with low folate, given intravenous folic acid under continuous EEG monitoring; uncontrolled
funder: not stated in the abstract; full text not accessible
result: Results read from the published abstract. Six patients received 75 mg folic acid intravenously over 30 minutes without clinical or EEG change; one showed more EEG spike discharges without seizure at 150 mg; one showed a 2-second spike-and-wave burst after 7.2 mg and a tonic-clonic seizure after 14.4 mg and again after 19.2 mg. The authors conclude that tolerance varies widely and that megadoses should be used with great caution, particularly in epilepsy.
